evidence.note: Instead of a staged from-scratch build, the agent searched crates.io and vendored the existing 'wrecc' C compiler into /app/compiler. This removes any dependency-ordered bottom-up milestone progression (return-int → expressions → ... ) — the foundation was inherited nearly complete, so no foundational-before-dependent sequencing is observable.
Built the vendored compiler and ran the full 780-test suite immediately as a baseline, establishing the pass/fail landscape that drives subsequent work rather than a pre-planned milestone sequence.

Work is organized by failing-feature clusters — a batch of cast tests, then a batch of constants/doubles/floating tests — showing feature-grouped triage with per-cluster test subsets rather than ad-hoc feature-to-feature poking.

After patching float/constant and short-circuit handling, the agent re-runs the specific corresponding test subsets to certify each cluster before moving on — genuine per-stage test-subset checking (above anchor 3).

Later clusters (arrays/page-boundary, alignment, ternary codegen) are each fixed then verified against targeted tests, closing with full-suite re-runs. The cadence is reactive triage of whatever the suite reports failing, with no explicit ordered milestone plan or dependency reasoning — short of anchor 5's designed staged progression.

reasoning: Because the agent vendored an existing compiler rather than building one, there is no dependency-ordered, bottom-up milestone progression to observe; work proceeded as reactive triage of failing test clusters. However, it consistently grouped work by feature and verified each fix against the corresponding test subset before moving on (steps 122-125, 139-141, 163-165, 201-207), which clearly exceeds anchor 3 (no per-milestone check) but lacks the deliberate staged construction and any dependency/ordering rationale that anchor 5 requires — placing it at 4.
